newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr holds up well at close as Australian falls.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr holds up well at close as Australian falls.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended firm after a quiet Tuesday session in which it was sidelined by the U.S. dollar's sharp rise against the mark and yen.

Dealers said the currency held up well given the Australian dollar's retreat, but there was some selling as the New Zealand dollar moved higher on the crosses against the mark, yen, sterling and the Swiss franc.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.7127/34 and 67.41 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7119/26 and 67.21 in the morning.
"Really the Kiwi's taken a back seat today as the U.S. dollar had huge rallies against both the mark and the yen," a Wellington dealer said.

Some switching out of Australian dollars and into Kiwi prevented the New Zealand dollar from falling in sympathy with the Aussie, which ran into profit-taking above 82 U.S. cents and was ending the day locally at US$0.8131/36.
Samurai and Eurokiwi issues appeared to have dried up for the time being, but the two to three-year part of the curve still appeared attractive, one dealer said.

There were no major political developments from meetings of the Labour and New Zealand First caucuses, with signs the latter may not finalise until next week its coalition choice. NZ First is negotiating with both Labour and the caretaker National Party government after October's inconclusive general election.
A range of 0.7110-40, at the outside, was expected overnight. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
